title: Read the recovered flag the right way round and pre-register exposure
hypothesis: The weekly provider segment and the shipped-record acceptance table both rested on a misread field: a `provider_error` incident carrying `final: true` counted as user-visible, while `final` was set when a usable answer closed the retry run. A second defect let a metric filter on the report bucket, which a trace span overwrites, so the qoder catalog baseline read 0.00 while eleven user-visible failures existed.
measurement: Same 28-day harvest as round 7: 715 sessions, 1,678 incidents, 4,178 user turns before the 2026-11-10T13:30:07Z switch. Provider table and weekly segment now share one predicate and one test.
result: The flag is renamed to `recovered` (true = a later usable answer closed the run) and both readers use it; openai-codex before the switch is 3.8 user-visible failures per 100 turns (104 events), not 19.8 (539, which were the recovered ones). Provider detail now keeps the provider's own `code` next to the trace bucket, so qoder catalog failures are countable: 11 user-visible events, baseline 0.263 per 100. Each acceptance record now declares the exposure where its baseline predicts ten events, and the parser refuses any other value.

title: Count a replay's own turns, and score it with the event's own check
hypothesis: The replay reported every tool call in the resumed session, which includes the whole restored branch, so a short replay inherited thousands of history calls. Without a deterministic check no run could be scored, so no event could be admitted or rejected.
measurement: One session with branch history before the cut and two new turns; one admitted 3-of-5 reproduction and one 2-of-5 rejection over the same fixture.
result: `newTurnStats` cuts at the incident entryId and counts assistant messages, tool calls by name, and input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite/totalTokens over the new turns only. `--check COMMAND` runs the event's own check inside the clone after each run with the same scrubbed environment and shim, with `REPLAY_TRANSCRIPT` and `REPLAY_WORKSPACE` available to the check and not to the agent: exit 0 pass, 1 the reported failure, anything else unknown. Admission is `reproduced (replay)` at three failing runs of five, `not-reproduced` at three passing, and stays `unknown` when unscoreable runs keep both sides below the threshold. Round 7's own replay artifacts were no longer on disk, so its reported call count could not be recomputed and is not restated here; the counts in this round's entries come from the new statistic. Daily-install acceptance provenance: switched at 2026-11-12T02:47:28Z to build 6a7e2b0848acf870ec73ba3a5fd3a720c0b83d74, dirty=false. This is a provenance start, not proof this mechanism shipped or improved; existing acceptance rules and historical evidence remain unchanged.

title: Replay a repeated read-only verification instruction (1)
hypothesis: A user who repeats a read-only verification instruction almost verbatim did not get it the first time: either the runtime never opened the two config files, or the answer omitted the collection channels, workspaceId or toolOutput the instruction named, or the run wrote to the checkout it was told not to touch.
measurement: Event: a short branch in one private project (unnamed here); frozen product 0.1.27-main.50ccdc87 (the event's own release was no longer installed), 5 sequential runs at the model the session used, short branch, machine otherwise idle. Check, written before the batch and stored only in the private loop directory: the clone's `git status --porcelain` must be empty and the run's output must name the trace and scry channels, the workspaceId and the toolOutput value.
result: 0 of 5 runs failed the check, so the event is not reproduced on this product: 6 new assistant messages, 6 read calls per run (input 41,936 · output 390 · cacheRead 40,960 · cacheWrite 0 per run). The deterministic check ran in every run and produced a verdict, so the negative is a measured negative and not a missing check. Caveat: the frozen product is a fallback newer than the release the session actually ran, so this says the instruction is satisfied today, not that the original window was fine. No current-version arm was needed because nothing reproduced.
